chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from some of our companions, from Dawud ibn Farqad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

A man came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, I left while my wife was menstruating, and I returned while she was pregnant.' He (peace be upon him and his family) said to him: 'Whom do you accuse?' He said: 'I accuse two men.' He (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Bring them.' So they were brought. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'If he is the son of this one, he will be born with the umbilical cord wrapped around his neck (qatat) like so and so.' He was born as the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said. His umbilical cord was placed on the people of his mother, and his inheritance was for them. And if anyone had said to him: 'O son of the fornicatress,' he would have been lashed with the legal penalty.

61 - Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Qummi, who said: Some of our companions wrote to me and I conveyed it to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'I am your ransom, what do you say about a man who had illicit relations with a woman, she became pregnant, and then he married her after the pregnancy, and she brought forth a child who was most similar in creation to him?' He (peace be upon him) wrote with his own hand and seal: 'The child belongs to the non-father (i.e., the husband) and does not inherit (from the biological father).'

key_terms.قَطَطاً: With the umbilical cord wrapped around the neck (a sign of specific paternity)
key_terms.لُحُوق: Attaching offspring to a father (legal attribution)
key_terms.لِلْغَيْرِ أَبِيهِ: For the non-father (attributed to the husband)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a child's inheritance when the mother was pregnant from another man before marriage?
ai.summary: This hadith elucidates the Shia jurisprudence of 'liqāʾ' (attributing lineage) by contrasting biological paternity with legal attribution; the first narration highlights the Prophet’s ability to identify the biological father through physical signs, while the second clarifies that in cases of polyandry or post-pregnancy marriage, the child is attributed to the 'ghayya' (the man who married her), excluding him from inheritance. Scholarly tradition emphasizes that 'al-waladu li-l-ghayya' ensures social stability by linking the child to the husband who assumes responsibility, even if the biological father is distinct. This ruling underscores the principle that lineage is primarily a legal construct for inheritance and marriage prohibitions, rather than solely a biological one.
